title.zh: 卷三百九十六 列傳第一百五十五 史浩 王淮 趙雄 權邦彥 程松 陳謙 張巖
title.en: Volume 396 Biographies 155: Shi Hao, Wang Huai, Zhao Xiong, Quan Bangyan, Cheng Song, Chen Qian, Zhang Yan
title.raw: 卷三百九十六 列傳第一百五十五 史浩 王淮 趙雄 權邦彥 程松 陳謙 張巖 Volume 396 Biographies 155: Shi Hao, Wang Huai, Zhao Xiong, Quan Bangyan, Cheng Song, Chen Qian, Zhang Yan

sentences.zh: 史浩，字直翁，明州鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Shi Hao, styled Zhiweng, was a native of Yin County in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hao, courtesy name Zhiweng, came from Yin County in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興十四年登進士第，調紹興餘姚縣尉，歷溫州教授，郡守張九成器之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Yuyao County in Shaoxing, served as professor at Wenzhou, and the prefect Zhang Jiucheng regarded him highly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Shaoxing era (1144), he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Yuyao County in Shaoxing. He later served as professor at Wenzhou, where Prefect Zhang Jiucheng held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除太學正，升國子博士。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was appointed director of the Imperial University and promoted to erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he was appointed director of the Imperial University and then promoted to erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 因轉對，言：「普安、恩平二王宜擇其一以係天下望。」

translations.literal: On a rotating audience with the emperor, he said: "Of the two princes, Pu'an and Enping, one should be chosen to hold the hopes of the empire."
translations.idiomatic: During a rotating audience with the emperor, he said, "One of the two princes, Pu'an and Enping, should be chosen to anchor the hopes of the realm."

sentences.zh: 高宗頷之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong nodded in assent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 翌日，語大臣曰：「浩有用才也。」

translations.literal: The next day, he told the chief ministers: "Hao has useful talent."
translations.idiomatic: The following day he told his senior ministers, "Hao has real talent."

sentences.zh: 除秘書省校書郎兼二王府教授。

translations.literal: [Hao] was appointed as collator in the Secretariat and concurrently as instructor to both princely households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator in the Secretariat and concurrently instructor to both princely households.

sentences.zh: 三十年，普安郡王為皇子，進封建王，除浩權建王府教授。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Prince of Pu'an was made a prince, was promoted to Prince of Jian, and Hao was appointed acting instructor to the Prince of Jian's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1160), the Prince of Pu'an was made imperial son and promoted to Prince of Jian; Hao was appointed acting instructor to his household.

sentences.zh: 詔建王府置直講、贊讀各一員，浩守司封郎官兼直講。

translations.literal: An edict established the Prince of Jian's household with one lecturer and one reader each; Hao retained his post as bureau director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently served as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Prince of Jian's household established with one lecturer and one reader; Hao remained bureau director in the Department of State Affairs and also served as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 一日講《周禮》，言：「膳夫掌膳羞之事，歲終則會，惟王及后、世子之膳羞不會。

translations.literal: One day lecturing on the Rites of Zhou, he said: "The steward of provisions manages the affairs of meals; at year's end accounts are settled, except that the king's, queen's, and heir's provisions are not reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: One day, lecturing on the Rites of Zhou, he said, "The steward of provisions oversees meals; at year's end accounts are settled—but the king's, the queen's, and the heir apparent's provisions are not counted.

sentences.zh: 至酒正掌飲酒之事，歲終則會，惟王及后之飲酒不會，世子不與焉。

translations.literal: As for the director of wine who manages drinking matters, at year's end accounts are settled, except the king's and queen's drinking is not reckoned; the heir is not included.
translations.idiomatic: As for the director of wine, who oversees drinking, accounts are settled at year's end—except for the king's and queen's wine; the heir apparent is not included.

sentences.zh: 以是知世子膳羞可以不會，世子飲酒不可以無節也。」

translations.literal: From this one knows that the heir's provisions need not be reckoned, but the heir's drinking must not be without moderation."
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that while the heir's meals need not be counted, his drinking may not go unrestrained."

sentences.zh: 王作而謝曰：「敢不佩斯訓。」

translations.literal: The prince rose and thanked him: "How dare I not accept this lesson."
translations.idiomatic: The prince rose and thanked him, saying, "I shall heed this instruction."

sentences.zh: 三十一年，遷宗正少卿。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was transferred to be vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1161), he was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 會金主亮犯邊，下詔親征。

translations.literal: At this time the Jin ruler Haiming invaded the border, and an edict was issued for the emperor to lead the campaign personally.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor Haiming invaded the frontier, an edict ordered the emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮失守，廷臣爭陳退避計，建王抗疏請率師為前驅。

translations.literal: At that time both Huai regions were lost, court officials vied to propose retreat plans, and the Prince of Jian submitted a bold memorial asking to lead troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: With both Huai regions lost, court officials competed in urging retreat, but the Prince of Jian submitted a bold memorial asking to lead the army as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 浩為王力言：「太子不可將兵，以晉申生、唐肅宗靈武之事為戒。」

translations.literal: Hao spoke forcefully to the prince: "The crown prince must not command troops; take warning from the cases of Shensheng of Jin and Emperor Suzong at Lingwu."
translations.idiomatic: Hao spoke emphatically to the prince: "A crown prince must not command troops—remember Shensheng of Jin and Tang Suzong at Lingwu."

sentences.zh: 王大感悟，立俾浩草奏，請扈蹕以供子職，辭意懇到。

translations.literal: The prince was deeply moved and immediately had Hao draft a memorial requesting to accompany the imperial retinue in performing filial duties, with earnest and sincere wording.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the prince had Hao draft a memorial at once, asking to accompany the emperor in filial service; its language was earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 高宗方怒，覽奏意頓釋，知奏出於浩，語大臣曰：「真王府官也。」

translations.literal: Gaozong was just then angry; upon reading the memorial his anger immediately eased. Learning the memorial came from Hao, he told the ministers: "A true household official of the prince."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong had been angry, but reading the memorial his mood softened at once. When he learned Hao had drafted it, he told his ministers, "That is a true servant of the prince's household."

sentences.zh: 既而殿中侍御史吳芾乞以皇子為元帥，先視師。

translations.literal: Soon after, the palace censor Wu Bi requested that the prince be made commander-in-chief to inspect the army first.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Palace Censor Wu Bi asked that the prince be made commander-in-chief and sent ahead to inspect the troops.

sentences.zh: 浩復遺大臣書，言：「建王生深宮中，未嘗與諸將接，安能辦此。」

translations.literal: Hao again sent letters to the chief ministers, saying: "The Prince of Jian was born in the inner palace and has never dealt with the generals; how could he manage this?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao again wrote to the senior ministers, saying, "The Prince of Jian was raised in the inner palace and has never worked with the generals—how could he handle such a task?"

sentences.zh: 或謂使王居守，浩復以為不可。

translations.literal: Some suggested having the prince remain to guard the capital, but Hao again held this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed leaving the prince behind to guard the capital, Hao again objected.

sentences.zh: 上亦欲令王遍識諸將，遂扈蹕如建康。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to have the prince become acquainted with all the generals, so he accompanied the retinue to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wanted the prince to meet the generals in person, so he accompanied the imperial retinue to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，上還臨安，立建王為皇太子，浩除起居郎兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the emperor returned to Lin'an, established the Prince of Jian as crown prince, and Hao was appointed as diarist and concurrently right vice tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year (1162), the emperor returned to Lin'an, made the Prince of Jian crown prince, and appointed Hao diarist and right vice tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，遂以中書舍人遷翰林學士、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, [Hao] was transferred from drafter in the Secretariat to Hanlin academician and controller of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Hao rose from drafter in the Secretariat to Hanlin academician and controller of edicts.

sentences.zh: 張浚宣撫江、淮，將圖恢復，浩與之異議，欲城瓜洲、采石。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was pacification commissioner for the Jiang and Huai regions and planned recovery; Hao disagreed and wished to fortify Guazhou and Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, pacification commissioner for the Jiang and Huai regions, planned to recover lost territory, but Hao disagreed and favored fortifying Guazhou and Caishi instead.

sentences.zh: 浚奏：「不守兩淮而守江，不若城泗州。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun memorialized: "Rather than not holding the two Huai regions and defending the Yangzi, it would be better to fortify Sizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun memorialized, "If we abandon the two Huai regions and defend only the Yangzi, we would do better to fortify Sizhou."

sentences.zh: 除參知政事。

translations.literal: [Hao] was appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 有詔議應敵定論，洪遵、金安節、唐文若等相繼論列，宰執獨無奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered discussion of a settled policy for meeting the enemy; Hong Zun, Jin Anjie, Tang Wenruo, and others submitted opinions in succession, but the chief ministers alone submitted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for debate on a settled policy against the enemy. Hong Zun, Jin Anjie, Tang Wenruo, and others submitted opinions in turn, but the chief ministers offered none.

sentences.zh: 上以問浩，浩奏：「先為備禦，是謂良規。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Hao, and Hao memorialized: "To prepare defenses first is the sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao, who replied, "Preparing defenses first is the sound policy.

sentences.zh: 儻聽淺謀之士，興不教之師，寇去則論賞以邀功，寇至則斂兵而遁跡，謂之恢復得乎？」

translations.literal: If one listens to shallow schemers, raises an untrained army, rewards merit when the enemy withdraws, and hides troops when the enemy arrives, can this be called recovery?"
translations.idiomatic: If we heed shallow schemers, raise an untrained army, hand out rewards when the enemy withdraws, and hide our troops when they return—can that be called recovery?"

sentences.zh: 薦樞密院編修官陸游、尹穡，召對，並賜出身。

translations.literal: He recommended Lu You and Yin Ji, compilers at the Bureau of Military Affairs; they were summoned for audience and both granted official status.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Lu You and Yin Ji, compilers at the Bureau of Military Affairs; both were summoned for audience and granted official status.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，拜尚書右僕射，首言趙鼎、李光之無罪，岳飛之久冤，宜復其官爵，祿其子孫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and first stated that Zhao Ding and Li Guang were innocent and that Yue Fei had long been wronged; their ranks should be restored and their descendants granted stipends.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing (1163), he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and first argued that Zhao Ding and Li Guang were innocent and that Yue Fei had long been wronged; their ranks should be restored and their descendants given stipends.

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 李顯忠、邵宏淵奏乞引兵進取，浩奏：「二將輒乞戰，豈督府命令有不行耶？」

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan memorialized requesting to lead troops in an advance; Hao memorialized: "These two generals presumptuously ask to fight—are the pacification headquarters' orders not being obeyed?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong and Shao Hongyuan memorialized asking to lead troops forward. Hao replied, "These two generals are begging to fight on their own—are the pacification headquarters' orders no longer obeyed?"

sentences.zh: 浚請入覲，乞即日降詔幸建康，上以問浩，浩陳三說不可，退，又以詰浚曰：「帝王之兵，當出萬全，豈可嘗試以圖僥倖。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun requested an audience and asked that an edict be issued at once for the emperor to visit Jiankang. The emperor asked Hao, who set forth three reasons why this could not be done. After retiring, he again questioned Zhang Jun: "An emperor's army must proceed with complete safety; how can one make trial sorties hoping for luck?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun requested an audience and asked that an edict be issued at once for the emperor to visit Jiankang. The emperor consulted Hao, who gave three reasons against it. After retiring, he pressed Zhang Jun: "An emperor's army must be deployed with complete safety—how can we gamble on a lucky strike?"

sentences.zh: 復辨論於殿上，浚曰：「中原久陷，今不取，豪傑必起而收之。」

translations.literal: They debated again in the hall. Zhang Jun said: "The Central Plains have long been lost; if we do not take them now, heroes will rise and seize them."
translations.idiomatic: They debated again in court. Zhang Jun said, "The Central Plains have been lost for years; if we do not recover them now, local heroes will rise and take them."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「中原決無豪傑，若有之，何不起而亡金？」

translations.literal: Hao said: "There are certainly no heroes in the Central Plains; if there were, why have they not risen and destroyed Jin?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "There are no such heroes in the Central Plains—if there were, why have they not risen and overthrown the Jin?"

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「彼民間無寸鐵，不能自起，待我兵至為內應。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said: "The people there have not even a foot of iron and cannot rise on their own; they wait for our troops to arrive as inside collaborators."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said, "The people there are unarmed and cannot rise on their own; they are waiting for our army to arrive and act as allies within."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「勝、廣以鉏櫌棘矜亡秦，必待我兵，非豪傑矣。」

translations.literal: Hao said: "Chen Sheng and Wu Guang overthrew Qin with hoes and thorn branches; if they had to wait for our troops, they would not have been heroes."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Chen Sheng and Wu Guang overthrew Qin with hoes and thorn branches—if heroes had to wait for our army, they would not be heroes at all."

sentences.zh: 浚因內引奏：「浩意不可回，恐失幾會，乞出英斷。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun then submitted privately: "Hao's mind cannot be changed; I fear we will miss the opportunity. I beg Your Majesty to issue a resolute decision."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun then submitted privately, "Hao's mind cannot be changed; I fear we will miss our chance. I beg Your Majesty to decide resolutely."

sentences.zh: 省中忽得宏淵出兵狀，始知不由三省，徑檄諸將。

translations.literal: The Secretariat suddenly received Hongyuan's troop deployment report and only then learned that orders had not gone through the Three Departments but had been sent directly to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat suddenly received Hongyuan's troop deployment report and learned that orders had bypassed the Three Departments and gone straight to the generals.

sentences.zh: 浩語陳康伯曰：「吾屬俱兼右府，而出兵不與聞，焉用相哉！

translations.literal: Hao said to Chen Kangbo: "We all concurrently serve in the right office, yet we were not informed of troop deployment—what use are we as councilors!
translations.idiomatic: Hao said to Chen Kangbo, "We all serve concurrently in the right office, yet we were not told about troop deployment—what use are we as councilors?

sentences.zh: 不去尚何待乎？」

translations.literal: If we do not leave, what are we waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: If we do not resign, what are we waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 因又言：「康伯欲納歸正人，臣恐他日必為陛下子孫憂。

translations.literal: He also said: "Kangbo wishes to accept defectors from Jin; I fear this will one day become a worry for Your Majesty's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Kangbo wants to accept defectors from Jin; I fear that will one day trouble Your Majesty's descendants.

sentences.zh: 浚銳意用兵，若一失之後，恐陛下終不得復望中原。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun is intent on using troops; if there is one failure, I fear Your Majesty will never again be able to hope for the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun is set on war; after one defeat, I fear Your Majesty will never again be able to hope for the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 御史王十朋論之，出知紹興。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Shipeng criticized this, and [Hao] was sent out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Shipeng impeached him, and Hao was sent out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 先是，浩因城瓜洲，白遣太府丞史正志往視之，正志與浚論辯。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Hao was fortifying Guazhou, he reported and sent the vice director of the Palace Storehouse Shi Zhengzhi to inspect it; Zhengzhi debated with Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Hao was fortifying Guazhou, he reported this and sent Palace Storehouse Vice Director Shi Zhengzhi to inspect the work; Zhengzhi debated the matter with Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 十朋亦疏史正志朋比，並及浩，遂與祠，自是不召者十三年。

translations.literal: Wang Shipeng also memorialized that Shi Zhengzhi was forming factions and implicated Hao as well; [Hao] was then given a stipendary post, and from then on was not summoned for thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shipeng also memorialized that Shi Zhengzhi was forming factions and implicated Hao as well. Hao was given a stipendary post and was not summoned again for thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 起知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Shaoxing and pacification commissioner of eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Shaoxing and pacification commissioner of Eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 持母喪歸，服闋，知福州。

translations.literal: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended, he served as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，上問執政：「久不見史浩，無他否？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, the emperor asked the chief ministers: "I have not seen Shi Hao for a long time—is there anything else wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunxi era, the emperor asked the chief ministers, "I have not seen Shi Hao in a long time—is there any other reason?"

sentences.zh: 遂除少保、觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was then appointed junior guardian, grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, commissioner of the Liquan Abbey, and concurrently imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed junior guardian, grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, commissioner of the Liquan Abbey, and concurrently imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 五年，復為右丞相。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again became right chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1178), he again became right chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「自葉衡罷，虛席以待卿久矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since Ye Heng was dismissed, the seat has been left vacant waiting for you for a long time."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since Ye Heng was dismissed, this seat has been kept open for you a long time."

sentences.zh: 浩奏：「蒙恩再相，唯盡公道，庶無朋黨之弊。」

translations.literal: Hao memorialized: "Receiving grace to serve again as councilor, I will devote myself solely to public fairness, hoping to avoid the evil of faction."
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "Having received the grace to serve again as councilor, I will devote myself solely to public fairness, so that factionalism may be avoided."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相豈當有黨，人主亦不當以朋黨名臣下。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How should a chief councilor have a faction? A ruler also should not label his ministers as faction members.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Should a chief councilor have a faction? A ruler should not label his ministers as faction members.

sentences.zh: 朕但取賢者用之，否則去之。」

translations.literal: I simply employ the worthy; if not, I remove them."
translations.idiomatic: I simply employ the worthy; if they are not worthy, I remove them."

sentences.zh: 樞密都承旨王抃建議以殿、步二司軍多虛額，請各募三千人充之。

translations.literal: Wang Bian, chief receptionist at the Bureau of Military Affairs, proposed that the Palace and Infantry Commands had many phantom rolls and requested recruiting three thousand men for each to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian, chief receptionist at the Bureau of Military Affairs, proposed that the Palace and Infantry Commands had many phantom rolls on their registers and asked to recruit three thousand men for each command to fill them.

sentences.zh: 已而殿前司輒捕市人，京城騷動，被掠者多斷指，示不可用。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Palace Command arbitrarily seized townspeople; the capital was in turmoil, and many of those seized cut off their fingers to show they were unfit for service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Palace Command began seizing townspeople at will. The capital was thrown into turmoil, and many of those seized cut off their fingers to show they were unfit for service.

sentences.zh: 軍人怙眾，因奪民財。

translations.literal: The soldiers relied on their numbers and seized the people's property.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers, relying on their numbers, seized civilians' property.

sentences.zh: 浩奏：「盡釋所捕，而禽軍民首喧呶者送獄。」

translations.literal: Hao memorialized: "Release all those seized, and arrest the leading soldiers and civilians who caused the uproar and send them to prison."
translations.idiomatic: Hao memorialized, "Release all those seized, and arrest the leading soldiers and civilians who stirred up the uproar and send them to prison."

sentences.zh: 獄成議罪，欲取兵民各一人梟首以徇。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded and punishment was debated, it was proposed to take one soldier and one civilian each and behead them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded and punishment was debated, officials proposed executing one soldier and one civilian by decapitation as a warning.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「諸軍掠人奪貨至於哄，則始釁者軍人也，軍法從事固當。

translations.literal: Hao said: "When the troops plundered people and seized goods to the point of riot, the soldiers were the ones who started the trouble; military law should indeed be applied to them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "When the troops plundered people and seized goods until a riot broke out, the soldiers started the trouble; military law should indeed be applied to them.

sentences.zh: 若市人陸慶童特與抗鬥爾，可同罰乎？

translations.literal: But the townsman Lu Qingtong merely fought back in resistance—can he be punished the same way?
translations.idiomatic: But the townsman Lu Qingtong merely fought back in resistance—can he be punished the same way?

sentences.zh: 陛下恐軍人有語，故一其罪以安之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fears the soldiers will complain, so you equalize their crimes to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty fears the soldiers will complain, so you are equalizing their crimes to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 夫民不得其平，言亦可畏，'等死，死國可乎？

translations.literal: When the people cannot obtain fairness, their words are also to be feared: 'Since death is the same either way, shall we die for the state?'
translations.idiomatic: When the people cannot obtain justice, their words are also to be feared: 'Since death is the same either way, shall we die for the state?'

sentences.zh: '是豈軍人語。」

translations.literal: Is that the speech of soldiers?"
translations.idiomatic: Is that the speech of soldiers?"

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「是比朕為秦二世也。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "This compares me to Qin Er Shi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, "You are comparing me to Qin Er Shi."

sentences.zh: 浩徐進曰：「自古民怨其上者多矣，『時日曷喪，予及汝偕亡』，豈二世事。」

translations.literal: Hao slowly advanced and said: "From antiquity there have been many cases of the people resenting their rulers; 'The day is come—let us perish together with you'—was that only a matter of the second [Qin emperor]?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied calmly, "From antiquity many rulers have faced popular resentment; 'The day is come—let us perish together with you'—was that only a matter of the second Qin emperor?"

sentences.zh: 尋求去，拜少傅、保寧軍節度使，充醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon after he requested to leave office and was appointed junior tutor, military commissioner of Baoning Army, and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey, concurrently imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to leave office and was appointed junior tutor, military commissioner of the Baoning Army, and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey, concurrently imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 後有言慶童之冤者，上曰：「史浩嘗力爭，坐此求去，至今悔之。」

translations.literal: Later, when someone spoke of Qingtong's injustice, the emperor said: "Shi Hao once argued forcefully on this account and resigned because of it; I regret that to this day."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when someone spoke of Qingtong's injustice, the emperor said, "Shi Hao once argued forcefully on this and resigned because of it—I regret that to this day."

sentences.zh: 趙雄嘗薦劉光祖試館職，光祖答策，論科場取士之道，進入，上親批其後，略曰：「用人之弊，人君乏知人之哲，宰相不能擇人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiong once recommended Liu Guangzu for a trial post in the Hanlin Academy; Guangzu answered the examination question discussing the way of selecting scholars through the civil service examinations. When it was submitted, the emperor personally annotated it afterward, saying in summary: "The flaw in employing men is that the ruler lacks the wisdom to know men and the chief councilor cannot choose men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong once recommended Liu Guangzu for a trial Hanlin post. Guangzu's examination answer discussed how scholars were selected through the civil service examinations. When it was submitted, the emperor personally annotated it, writing in summary, "The flaw in employing men is that the ruler lacks the wisdom to know men and the chief councilor cannot choose them.

sentences.zh: 國朝以來，過於忠厚，宰相而誤國，大將而敗軍，未嘗誅戮。

translations.literal: Since the founding of our dynasty we have been excessively generous and lenient; chief councilors who harmed the state and great generals who lost armies have never been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of our dynasty we have been excessively lenient; chief councilors who harmed the state and great generals who lost armies have never been executed.

sentences.zh: 要在人君必審擇相，相必當為官擇人，懋賞立乎前，誅戮設乎後，人才不出，吾不信也。」

translations.literal: The key is that the ruler must carefully choose his councilor, the councilor must choose officials for the posts, rich rewards stand before them and executions stand behind them—if talent does not emerge, I do not believe it."
translations.idiomatic: The key is that the ruler must carefully choose his councilor, the councilor must choose the right officials, rich rewards must stand before them and executions behind them—if talent still does not emerge, I do not believe it."

sentences.zh: 手詔既出，中外大聳。

translations.literal: Once the handwritten edict was issued, court and country were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once the handwritten edict was issued, court and country were greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 議者謂曾覿視草，為光祖甲科發也。

translations.literal: Commentators said Zeng Di had drafted the edict to launch Guangzu as top examination graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said Zeng Di had drafted the edict to launch Guangzu as a top examination graduate.

sentences.zh: 上遣覿持示浩，浩奏：「唐、虞之世，四凶極惡，止於流竄，三考之法，不過黜陟，未嘗有誅戮之科。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Di to show it to Hao. Hao memorialized: "In the age of Tang and Yu, the four villains were extremely wicked yet were only banished; the law of three appraisals amounted to no more than demotion and promotion—there was never a category of execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Di to show it to Hao. Hao memorialized, "In the age of Tang and Yu, the four villains were extremely wicked yet were only banished; the law of three appraisals amounted to no more than demotion and promotion—there was never a category of execution.

sentences.zh: 誅戮大臣，秦、漢法也。

translations.literal: Executing high ministers is the law of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Executing high ministers is the law of Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 太祖制治以仁，待臣下以禮，列聖傳心，迨仁宗而德化隆洽，本朝之治，與三代同風，此祖宗家法也。

translations.literal: Taizu governed with benevolence and treated his ministers with ritual propriety; successive sages transmitted this spirit, and by Emperor Renzong virtue and transformation flourished together. The governance of our dynasty shares the same spirit as the Three Dynasties—this is the ancestral house law.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu governed with benevolence and treated his ministers with ritual propriety; successive emperors transmitted this spirit, and by Emperor Renzong virtue and transformation flourished together. The governance of our dynasty shares the spirit of the Three Dynasties—this is our ancestral house law.

sentences.zh: 聖訓則曰過於忠厚。

translations.literal: The sacred instruction then says 'excessively generous and lenient.'
translations.idiomatic: The sacred instruction then says we are 'excessively lenient.'

sentences.zh: 夫為國而底于忠厚，豈有所謂過哉？

translations.literal: For governing a state to rest upon generosity and leniency—how can there be what is called excess?
translations.idiomatic: For a state to rest upon leniency—how can there be such a thing as excess?

sentences.zh: 臣恐議者以陛下自欲行刻薄之政，歸過祖宗，不可不審也。」

translations.literal: I fear commentators will say Your Majesty himself wishes to pursue harsh government and shift the blame onto the ancestors—this must be carefully considered."
translations.idiomatic: I fear commentators will say Your Majesty himself wishes to pursue harsh government and shift the blame onto the ancestors—this must be carefully considered."

sentences.zh: 及自經筵將告歸，乃於小官中薦江、浙之士十五人，有旨令升擢，皆一時選也。

translations.literal: When he was about to leave the Classics Mat and request retirement, he recommended fifteen scholars from Jiang and Zhe among lower officials; an edict ordered their promotion—all were outstanding selections of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to leave the Classics Mat and request retirement, he recommended fifteen scholars from Jiang and Zhe among lower officials; an edict ordered their promotion—all were outstanding men of the day.

sentences.zh: 如薛叔似、楊簡、陸九淵、石宗昭、陳謙、葉適、袁燮、趙靜之、張子智，後皆擢用，不至通顯者六人而已。

translations.literal: Such men as Xue Shusi, Yang Jian, Lu Jiuyuan, Shi Zongzhao, Chen Qian, Ye Shi, Yuan Xie, Zhao Jingzhi, and Zhang Zhizhi were later all promoted; only six did not reach high distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Xue Shusi, Yang Jian, Lu Jiuyuan, Shi Zongzhao, Chen Qian, Ye Shi, Yuan Xie, Zhao Jingzhi, and Zhang Zhizhi were later all promoted; only six did not reach high distinction.

sentences.zh: 十年，請老，除太保致仕，封魏國公。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he requested retirement on account of age and was appointed grand guardian with permission to retire, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1183), he requested retirement on account of age and was appointed grand guardian with permission to retire, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 晚治第鄞之西湖上，建閣奉兩朝賜書，又作堂，上為書「明良慶會」名其閣、「舊學」名其堂。

translations.literal: In his later years he built a residence on West Lake in Yin, erected a pavilion to house books bestowed by two reigns, and also built a hall; the emperor wrote 'Bright Ruler and Worthy Minister in Joyful Assembly' to name the pavilion and 'Former Studies' to name the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he built a residence on West Lake in Yin, erected a pavilion to house books bestowed by two reigns, and also built a hall; the emperor wrote "Bright Ruler and Worthy Minister in Joyful Assembly" to name the pavilion and "Former Studies" to name the hall.

sentences.zh: 光宗御極，進太師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, [Hao] was promoted to grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Hao was promoted to grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年薨，年八十九，封會稽郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he died at age eighty-nine and was enfeoffed as Prince of Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxi (1194) he died at age eighty-nine and was enfeoffed as Prince of Kuaiji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寧宗登極，賜諡「文惠」，御書「純誠厚德元老之碑」賜焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, he was granted the posthumous title 'Cultured and Kind' and bestowed an imperial inscription reading 'Stele for the Elder of Pure Sincerity and Deep Virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, he was granted the posthumous title "Cultured and Kind" and bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Stele for the Elder of Pure Sincerity and Deep Virtue."

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年，追封越王，改諡「忠定」，配享孝宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yue, his posthumous title was changed to 'Loyal and Settled,' and he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Xiaozong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiading (1221), he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yue, his posthumous title was changed to "Loyal and Settled," and he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Xiaozong's temple.

sentences.zh: 浩喜薦人才，嘗擬陳之茂進職與郡，上知之茂嘗毀浩，曰：「卿豈以德報怨耶？」

translations.literal: Hao liked recommending talent. He once proposed promoting Chen Zhimao to office and to a prefecture. The emperor knew Zhimao had once slandered Hao and said: "Are you repaying injury with virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao liked recommending talent. He once proposed promoting Chen Zhimao to office and to a prefecture. The emperor knew Zhimao had once slandered Hao and asked, "Are you repaying injury with virtue?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「臣不知有怨，若以為怨而以德報之，是有心也。」

translations.literal: Hao said: "Your servant knows nothing of injury; if one treats it as injury and repays it with virtue, that is calculation."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "I know nothing of any injury; if one treats it as injury and repays it with virtue, that is calculation."

sentences.zh: 莫濟狀王十朋行事，詆浩尤甚，浩薦濟掌內制，上曰：「濟非議卿者乎？」

translations.literal: Mo Ji submitted a report on Wang Shipeng's conduct that criticized Hao especially harshly; Hao recommended Ji to manage inner edicts. The emperor said: "Was not Ji among those who criticized you?"
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ji submitted a report on Wang Shipeng's conduct that criticized Hao especially harshly; Hao recommended Ji to manage inner edicts. The emperor said, "Was not Ji among those who criticized you?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「臣不敢以私害公。」

translations.literal: Hao said: "Your servant dare not let private feeling harm the public good."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "I dare not let private feeling harm the public good."

sentences.zh: 遂除中書舍人兼直學士院，待之如初。

translations.literal: Ji was then appointed drafter in the Secretariat and concurrently director of the Hanlin Academy; [Hao] treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then appointed drafter in the Secretariat and concurrently director of the Hanlin Academy; Hao treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 蓋其寬厚類此。

translations.literal: His generosity and forbearance were generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His generosity and forbearance were generally of this kind.

sentences.zh: 子：彌大、彌正、彌遠、彌堅。

translations.literal: His sons were: Midà, Mizheng, Miyuan, and Mijian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Midà, Mizheng, Miyuan, and Mijian.

sentences.zh: 彌遠嘉定初為右丞相，有傳。

translations.literal: Miyuan became right chief councilor at the beginning of Jiading; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan became right chief councilor at the beginning of Jiading; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王淮，字季海，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Wang Huai, styled Jihai, was a native of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai, courtesy name Jihai, came from Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，力學屬文。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick-witted and perceptive, studied diligently, and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick-witted and perceptive, studied diligently, and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 登紹興十五年進士第，為台州臨海尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Shaoxing and served as assistant magistrate of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Shaoxing (1145) and was appointed assistant magistrate of Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守蕭振一見奇之，許以公輔器。

translations.literal: The prefect Xiao Zhen was struck by him at first sight and declared him material for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xiao Zhen was struck by him at first sight and declared him material for chief minister.

sentences.zh: 振帥蜀，辟置幕府。

translations.literal: When Zhen commanded Shu, he recruited [Huai] into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen took command of Shu, he recruited Huai into his staff.

sentences.zh: 振出，眾欲留，淮曰：「萬里將母，豈為利祿計。」

translations.literal: When Zhen departed, the others wished to keep [Huai]; Huai said: "I am taking my mother a thousand li—how could I be calculating profit and salary?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen departed, the others wished to keep Huai behind; Huai said, "I am taking my mother a thousand li—how could I be calculating profit and salary?"

sentences.zh: 皆服其器識，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: All admired his capacity and judgment, and he was transferred to collator.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his capacity and judgment, and he was transferred to collator.

sentences.zh: 高宗命中丞舉可為御史者，朱倬舉淮，除監察御史，尋遷右正言。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered the vice censor-in-chief to recommend men fit to be censors; Zhu Zhuo recommended Huai, who was appointed investigating censor and soon transferred to right remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ordered the vice censor-in-chief to recommend men fit to serve as censors; Zhu Zhuo recommended Huai, who was appointed investigating censor and soon transferred to right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 首論：「大臣養尊，小臣持祿，以括囊為智，以引去為高。

translations.literal: He first argued: "Great ministers cultivate their dignity, petty officials hold their salaries, taking purse-closing as wisdom and withdrawal as elevation.
translations.idiomatic: He first argued, "Great ministers cultivate their dignity, petty officials hold their salaries, taking purse-closing as wisdom and withdrawal as elevation.

sentences.zh: 願陛下正心以正朝廷，正朝廷以正百官。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to rectify the heart to rectify the court, and rectify the court to rectify the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to rectify the heart to rectify the court, and rectify the court to rectify the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 宰相湯思退無物望，淮條其罪數十，於是策免。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Tang Situi had no public esteem; Huai listed several dozen of his crimes, and Situi was then dismissed by imperial rescript.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Tang Situi had no public esteem; Huai listed several dozen of his crimes, and Situi was then dismissed by imperial rescript.

sentences.zh: 至於吏部侍郎沈介之欺世盜名，都司方師尹之狡險，大將劉寶掊克結權倖，皆劾罷之。

translations.literal: As for Vice Minister of Personnel Shen Jie's deceiving the world and stealing reputation, Bureau Director Fang Shiyin's craftiness and treachery, and Grand General Liu Bao's extortion and collusion with favored power-holders—all were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: As for Vice Minister of Personnel Shen Jie, who deceived the world and stole reputation; Bureau Director Fang Shiyin, who was crafty and treacherous; and Grand General Liu Bao, who extorted and colluded with favored power-holders—all were impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「自治之策，治內有三：正心術，寶慈儉，去壅蔽。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The policy for self-governance has three points for internal rule: rectify the mind and methods, treasure kindness and frugality, and remove obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "The policy for self-governance has three points for internal rule: rectify the mind and methods, treasure kindness and frugality, and remove obstruction and concealment.

sentences.zh: 治外有四：固封守，選將帥，明賞罰，儲財用。」

translations.literal: For external rule there are four: strengthen frontier defense, select generals and commanders, clarify rewards and punishments, and store up wealth and resources."
translations.idiomatic: For external rule there are four: strengthen frontier defense, select generals and commanders, clarify rewards and punishments, and store up wealth and resources."

sentences.zh: 上深嘉歎。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply praised and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 除秘書少監兼恭王府直講。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently lecturer to the Prince of Gong's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently lecturer to the Prince of Gong's household.

sentences.zh: 時恭王生子挺，淮白于丞相，曰：「恭王夫人李氏生皇嫡長孫，乞討論典禮。」

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Gong's wife Lady Li gave birth to Ting; Huai reported to the chief councilor, saying: "The Prince of Gong's consort Lady Li has borne the emperor's eldest legitimate grandson; I beg that the proper rites be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Gong's wife Lady Li gave birth to Ting; Huai reported to the chief councilor, saying, "The Prince of Gong's consort Lady Li has borne the emperor's eldest legitimate grandson; I beg that the proper rites be discussed."

sentences.zh: 錢端禮怒其名稱，奏：「淮有年鈞以長之說。」

translations.literal: Qian Duansli was angered by this title and memorialized: "Huai has the doctrine of using seniority to determine precedence."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Duansli was angered by this title and memorialized, "Huai has the doctrine of using seniority to determine precedence."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「是何言也，豈不啟邪心？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What kind of talk is this—does it not open the way to wicked intent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What kind of talk is this—does it not open the way to wicked intent?"

sentences.zh: 出淮知建寧府，改浙西提刑。

translations.literal: Huai was sent out to serve as prefect of Jianning and then changed to judicial commissioner of western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was sent out to serve as prefect of Jianning and then transferred to judicial commissioner of Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 入見，陳閩中利病甚悉。

translations.literal: On entering audience, he set forth the advantages and ills of Minzhong in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience, he set forth the advantages and ills of Fujian in great detail.

sentences.zh: 帝褒嘉之，且令一至東宮，皇太子待以師儒，特施拜禮。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and commended him, and also ordered him to visit the Eastern Palace once; the crown prince treated him as teacher and scholar, and a special bowing ceremony was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and commended him, and also ordered him to visit the Eastern Palace once; the crown prince treated him as teacher and scholar, and a special bowing ceremony was performed.

sentences.zh: 尋召，除太常少卿，除中書舍人兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Soon after he was recalled, appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed drafter in the Secretariat and concurrently director of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled, appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed drafter in the Secretariat and concurrently director of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 龍大淵贈太師，仍畀儀同三司恩數，張說除太尉、在京宮觀，皆封還詔書。

translations.literal: Long Dayuan was posthumously granted grand preceptor and still given the privileges of equal rank with the Three Excellencies; Zhang Yue was appointed grand marshal with a capital stipendary post—all edicts were sealed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Long Dayuan was posthumously granted grand preceptor and still given the privileges of equal rank with the Three Excellencies; Zhang Yue was appointed grand marshal with a capital stipendary post—all edicts were sealed and returned.

sentences.zh: 除翰林學士、知制誥，訓詞深厚，得王言體。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin academician and controller of edicts; his instruction edicts were profound and substantial, attaining the style of royal speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician and controller of edicts; his instruction edicts were profound and substantial, attaining the style of royal speech.

sentences.zh: 上命擇文學行誼之士，淮薦鄭伯熊、李燾、程叔達，皆擢用。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered selection of men of literary learning and moral conduct; Huai recommended Zheng Boxiong, Li Tao, and Cheng Shuda, and all were promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered selection of men of literary learning and moral conduct; Huai recommended Zheng Boxiong, Li Tao, and Cheng Shuda, and all were promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, he was appointed academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi (1175), he was appointed academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛棄疾平茶寇，上功太濫。

translations.literal: Xin Qiji pacified the tea bandits, but the reported merit was excessively generous.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji pacified the tea bandits, but the reported merit was excessively generous.

sentences.zh: 淮謂：「不核真偽，何以勸有功。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "If truth and falsehood are not verified, how can merit be rewarded?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "If truth and falsehood are not verified, how can merit be rewarded?"

sentences.zh: 文州蕃部擾邊，吳挺奏：「庫彥威失利，靖州夷人擾邊。」

translations.literal: Tribal groups in Wen Prefecture disturbed the border; Wu Ting memorialized: "Ku Yanwei suffered defeat, and the Yi people of Jing Prefecture are disturbing the border."
translations.idiomatic: Tribal groups in Wen Prefecture disturbed the border; Wu Ting memorialized, "Ku Yanwei suffered defeat, and the Yi people of Jing Prefecture are disturbing the border."

sentences.zh: 楊倓奏：「田淇失利。」

translations.literal: Yang Tan memorialized: "Tian Qi suffered defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tan memorialized, "Tian Qi suffered defeat."

sentences.zh: 淮謂：「二將戰歿，若罪之，何以勸來者。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "These two generals died in battle; if they are punished, how can those who come after be encouraged?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "These two generals died in battle; if they are punished, how can those who come after be encouraged?"

sentences.zh: 上嘗諭曰：「樞密臨事盡公，人無間言，差除能守法甚善。」

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed him: "At the Bureau of Military Affairs you handle affairs with complete fairness and no one speaks against you; in appointments you can uphold the law—this is very good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, "At the Bureau of Military Affairs you handle affairs with complete fairness and no one speaks against you; in appointments you can uphold the law—this is very good."

sentences.zh: 薦軍帥吳拱、郭田、張宣。

translations.literal: He recommended the military commanders Wu Gong, Guo Tian, and Zhang Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the military commanders Wu Gong, Guo Tian, and Zhang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 除同知樞密院事、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時宰相久虛，淮與李彥穎同行相事。

translations.literal: At that time the chief councilor's seat had long been vacant; Huai and Li Yanying jointly performed councilor duties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief councilor's seat had long been vacant; Huai and Li Yanying jointly performed councilor duties.

sentences.zh: 淮謂：「授官當論賢否，不事形跡。

translations.literal: Huai said: "In granting office one should judge worthiness or unworthiness, not outward appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "In granting office one should judge worthiness or unworthiness, not outward appearances.

sentences.zh: 誠賢，不敢以鄉里故舊廢之；

translations.literal: If truly worthy, one dare not dismiss him because of hometown ties or old friendship;
translations.idiomatic: If truly worthy, one dare not dismiss him because of hometown ties or old friendship;

sentences.zh: 非才，不敢以己私庇之。」

translations.literal: if lacking talent, one dare not shield him out of private feeling."
translations.idiomatic: if lacking talent, one dare not shield him out of private feeling."

sentences.zh: 上稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 擢知院事、樞密使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the bureau and commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the bureau and commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言武臣嶽祠之員宜省，淮曰：「有戰功者，壯用其力，老而棄之，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of reducing the quota of military officials in mountain temple stipendary posts; Huai said: "Those with battle merit used their strength in their prime—when old, to cast them aside, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke of reducing the quota of military officials in mountain temple stipendary posts; Huai said, "Those with battle merit used their strength in their prime—when old, to cast them aside, is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 趙雄言：「北人歸附者，畀以員外置，宜令詣吏部。」

translations.literal: Zhao Xiong said: "Northerners who have submitted should be given supernumerary appointments and ought to be ordered to report to the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong said, "Northerners who have submitted should be given supernumerary appointments and ought to be ordered to report to the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「姑仍舊。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For now, keep the old practice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For now, keep the old practice."

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「上意即天意也。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "Your Majesty's intent is Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "Your Majesty's intent is Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 雄又奏言：「宗室嶽祠八百員，宜罷。」

translations.literal: Xiong again memorialized: "There are eight hundred imperial clansmen in mountain temple stipendary posts—they should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong again memorialized, "There are eight hundred imperial clansmen in mountain temple stipendary posts—they should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「堯親睦九族，在平章百姓之先；

translations.literal: Huai said: "Yao treated the nine clans with kinship and harmony before he brought peace to the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "Yao treated the nine clans with kinship and harmony before he brought peace to the common people;

sentences.zh: 骨肉之恩疏，可乎？」

translations.literal: to make blood kin distant—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: to make blood kin distant—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 時辛棄疾平江西寇，王佐平湖南寇，劉焞平廣西寇，淮皆處置得宜，論功惟允。

translations.literal: At that time Xin Qiji pacified the bandits of Jiangxi, Wang Zuo those of Hunan, and Liu Chun those of Guangxi; Huai handled all these appropriately and judged merit fairly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xin Qiji pacified the bandits of Jiangxi, Wang Zuo those of Hunan, and Liu Chun those of Guangxi; Huai handled all these appropriately and judged merit fairly.

sentences.zh: 上深嘉之，謂：「陳康伯雖有人望，處事則不及卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised him, saying: "Chen Kangbo may have public esteem, but in handling affairs he does not match you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply praised him, saying, "Chen Kangbo may have public esteem, but in handling affairs he does not match you."

sentences.zh: 八年，拜右丞相兼樞密事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed right chief councilor and concurrently commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1181), he was appointed right chief councilor and concurrently commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，自夏不雨至秋，是日甘雨如注，士大夫相賀，上亦喜命相而雨，乃命口算諸郡絹錢盡蠲一年，為緡八十萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, from summer there had been no rain until autumn; on that day sweet rain poured down. The scholar-officials congratulated one another, and the emperor also rejoiced that rain came with the appointment of a councilor. He then ordered by oral calculation that silk-tax money in all prefectures be remitted for one year, amounting to eight hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, from summer there had been no rain until autumn; on that day sweet rain poured down. The scholar-officials congratulated one another, and the emperor also rejoiced that rain came with the appointment of a councilor. He then ordered that silk-tax money in all prefectures be remitted for one year, amounting to eight hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 趙雄罷相，蜀士之在朝者皆有去意。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xiong was dismissed as councilor, the Shu scholars at court all had thoughts of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xiong was dismissed as councilor, the Shu scholars at court all had thoughts of leaving.

sentences.zh: 淮謂：「此唐季黨禍之胎也，豈聖世所宜有。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "This is the seed of the factional disasters of late Tang—how can a sage age have such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "This is the seed of the factional disasters of late Tang—how can a sage age have such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 皆以次進遷，蜀士乃安。

translations.literal: All were promoted in turn by seniority, and the Shu scholars were then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: All were promoted in turn by seniority, and the Shu scholars were then reassured.

sentences.zh: 樞密都承旨王抃怙寵為姦，淮極陳其罪，謂：「人主受謗，鮮不由此。」

translations.literal: Wang Bian, chief receptionist at the Bureau of Military Affairs, relied on favor to commit wickedness; Huai fully set forth his crimes, saying: "When a ruler is slandered, rarely is it not because of such men."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian, chief receptionist at the Bureau of Military Affairs, relied on favor to commit wickedness; Huai fully set forth his crimes, saying, "When a ruler is slandered, rarely is it not because of such men."

sentences.zh: 上即斥之，且曰：「丞相直諒無隱，君臣之間正宜如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor immediately dismissed him and also said: "The chief councilor is direct, sincere, and without concealment—between ruler and minister this is exactly as it should be."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately dismissed him and also said, "The chief councilor is direct, sincere, and without concealment—between ruler and minister this is exactly as it should be."

sentences.zh: 章穎論事狂直，上將黜之，淮曰：「陛下樂聞直言，士大夫以言相高，此風可賀也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying discussed affairs with wild bluntness; the emperor was about to dismiss him. Huai said: "Your Majesty delights in hearing straight talk; scholar-officials take speech as their distinction—this custom is to be celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying discussed affairs with wild bluntness; the emperor was about to dismiss him. Huai said, "Your Majesty delights in hearing straight talk; scholar-officials take speech as their distinction—this custom is to be celebrated.

sentences.zh: 黜之適成其名。」

translations.literal: To dismiss him would only make his name."
translations.idiomatic: To dismiss him would only make his name."

sentences.zh: 上說，穎復留。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, and Ying was kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, and Ying was kept in office.

sentences.zh: 時以荒政為急，淮言：「李椿老成練達，擬除長沙帥，朱熹學行篤實，擬除浙東提舉，以倡郡國。」

translations.literal: At that time famine relief was urgent; Huai said: "Li Chun is experienced and seasoned—I propose appointing him commander of Changsha; Zhu Xi is solid in learning and conduct—I propose appointing him commissioner of eastern Zhe to lead the prefectures and commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: At that time famine relief was urgent; Huai said, "Li Chun is experienced and seasoned—I propose appointing him commander of Changsha; Zhu Xi is solid in learning and conduct—I propose appointing him commissioner of Eastern Zhe to lead the prefectures and commanderies."

sentences.zh: 其後推賞，上曰：「朱熹職事留意。」

translations.literal: Later, when merit was being recommended, the emperor said: "Zhu Xi attends carefully to his duties."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merit was being recommended, the emperor said, "Zhu Xi attends carefully to his duties."

sentences.zh: 淮言：「修舉荒政，是行其所學，民被實惠，欲與進職。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "In carrying out famine relief he is putting his learning into practice; the people have received real benefit—I wish to grant him advancement in rank."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "In carrying out famine relief he is putting his learning into practice; the people have received real benefit—I wish to grant him advancement in rank."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「與升直徽猷閣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Grant him promotion to the Direct Huayou Pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Grant him promotion to the Direct Huayou Pavilion."

sentences.zh: 成都闕帥，上加訪問，淮以留正對。

translations.literal: The Chengdu commander's post was vacant; the emperor further inquired, and Huai answered with Liu Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengdu commander's post was vacant; the emperor further inquired, and Huai answered with Liu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「非閩人乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is he not a man of Min?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is he not a man of Min?"

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「立賢無方，湯之執中也。

translations.literal: Huai said: "To establish the worthy without regard to origin—this is Tang's holding to the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "To establish the worthy without regard to origin—this is Tang's holding to the mean.

sentences.zh: 必曰閩有章子厚、呂惠卿，不有曾公亮、蘇頌、蔡襄乎？

translations.literal: Must one say that Min has Zhang Zihou and Lü Huiqing, and not Zeng Gongliang, Su Song, and Cai Xiang?
translations.idiomatic: Must one say that Min has Zhang Zihou and Lü Huiqing, and not Zeng Gongliang, Su Song, and Cai Xiang?

sentences.zh: 必曰江、浙多名臣，不有丁謂、王欽若乎？」

translations.literal: Must one say that Jiang and Zhe have many famous ministers, and not Ding Wei and Wang Qinruo?"
translations.idiomatic: Must one say that Jiang and Zhe have many famous ministers, and not Ding Wei and Wang Qinruo?"

sentences.zh: 上稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 拜左丞相。

translations.literal: He was appointed left chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 天長水害七十餘家，或謂不必以聞，淮曰：「昔人謂人主不可一日不聞水旱盜賊，《記》曰：『四方有敗，必先知之。』

translations.literal: At Tianchang, flooding harmed more than seventy households; some said it need not be reported. Huai said: "The ancients said a ruler must not go a single day without hearing of flood, drought, bandits, and thieves. The Record says: 'When there is disaster in the four directions, one must know of it first.'
translations.idiomatic: At Tianchang, flooding harmed more than seventy households; some said it need not be reported. Huai said, "The ancients said a ruler must not go a single day without hearing of flood, drought, bandits, and thieves. The Record says, 'When there is disaster in the four directions, one must know of it first.'

sentences.zh: 豈可不以聞？」

translations.literal: How can it not be reported?"
translations.idiomatic: How can it not be reported?"

sentences.zh: 鎮江饑民強借菽粟，執政請痛懲之，淮曰：「令甲，饑民罪不至死。」

translations.literal: In Zhenjiang, starving people forcibly borrowed beans and grain; the chief ministers requested severe punishment. Huai said: "By statute, starving people are not guilty of a capital crime."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjiang, starving people forcibly borrowed beans and grain; the chief ministers requested severe punishment. Huai said, "By statute, starving people are not guilty of a capital crime."

sentences.zh: 進士八人求以免舉恩為升等，淮曰：「八人得之，則百人援之。」

translations.literal: Eight jinshi degree holders requested exemption from examination favor for rank promotion; Huai said: "If eight obtain it, then a hundred will cite it as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Eight jinshi degree holders requested exemption from examination favor for rank promotion; Huai said, "If eight obtain it, then a hundred will cite it as precedent."

sentences.zh: 龔頤以執政之客補官，求詣銓曹，淮以此門不可啟，絕其請。

translations.literal: Gong Yi, as a client of the chief ministers, received office by patronage and requested an audience at the Board of Appointments; Huai held that this door must not be opened and rejected his request.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yi, as a client of the chief ministers, received office by patronage and requested an audience at the Board of Appointments; Huai held that this door must not be opened and rejected his request.

sentences.zh: 嘗言跅弛之士，緩急能出死力，乃以周極知安豐軍，辛棄疾與祠。

translations.literal: He once said that undisciplined men can in urgent need exert themselves unto death; accordingly he appointed Zhou Ji to command Anfeng Army and granted Xin Qiji a stipendary post.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that undisciplined men can in urgent need exert themselves unto death; accordingly he appointed Zhou Ji to command Anfeng Army and granted Xin Qiji a stipendary post.

sentences.zh: 上章力求去，以觀文殿大學士判衢州。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials repeatedly requesting to leave office and was appointed grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature with jurisdiction over Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials repeatedly requesting to leave office and was appointed grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature with jurisdiction over Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮力辭，改提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Huai forcefully declined and was changed to commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huai forcefully declined and was changed to commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 光宗嗣位，詔詢初政，淮以盡孝進德，奉天敬民，用人立政，罔不在初。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, an edict inquired about initial governance; Huai [advised] that fulfilling filial piety and advancing virtue, revering Heaven and respecting the people, employing men and establishing policy—all lie in the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, an edict inquired about initial governance; Huai advised that fulfilling filial piety and advancing virtue, revering Heaven and respecting the people, employing men and establishing policy—all lie in the beginning.

sentences.zh: 母亡，居喪如禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he observed mourning according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 得疾，忽語家人曰：「《易》卦六十四，吾年亦然。」

translations.literal: When he fell ill, he suddenly told his family: "The Book of Changes has sixty-four hexagrams—my years are likewise."
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he suddenly told his family, "The Book of Changes has sixty-four hexagrams—my years are likewise."

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年薨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi (1189) he died.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上哀悼，輟視朝，贈少師，諡「文定」。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor mourned, suspended court audience, posthumously granted him junior preceptor, and gave the posthumous title 'Literary and Settled.'
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the emperor mourned, suspended court audience, posthumously granted him junior preceptor, and gave the posthumous title "Literary and Settled."

sentences.zh: 初，朱熹為浙東提舉，劾知台州唐仲友。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhu Xi was commissioner of eastern Zhe, he impeached Tang Zhongyou, prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Xi was commissioner of Eastern Zhe, he impeached Tang Zhongyou, prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 淮素善仲友，不喜熹，乃擢陳賈為監察御史，俾上疏言：「近日道學假名濟偽之弊，請詔痛革之。」

translations.literal: Huai had long been on good terms with Zhongyou and disliked Xi; he therefore promoted Chen Jia to investigating censor and had him submit a memorial saying: "Recently the evil of the Learning of the Way using its name to cover falsehood—I beg that an edict sternly reform this."
translations.idiomatic: Huai had long been on good terms with Zhongyou and disliked Xi; he therefore promoted Chen Jia to investigating censor and had him submit a memorial saying, "Recently the Learning of the Way has used its name to cover falsehood—I beg that an edict sternly reform this."

sentences.zh: 鄭丙為吏部尚書，相與叶力攻道學，熹由此得祠。

translations.literal: Zheng Bing was minister of personnel; together they joined forces to attack the Learning of the Way, and Xi thereby received a stipendary post.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bing was minister of personnel; together they joined forces to attack the Learning of the Way, and Xi thereby received a stipendary post.

sentences.zh: 其後慶元偽學之禁始於此。

translations.literal: Afterward the Qingyuan prohibition against false learning began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Qingyuan prohibition against false learning began from this.

sentences.zh: 趙雄，字溫叔，資州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiong, styled Wenshu, was a native of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong, courtesy name Wenshu, came from Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 為隆興元年類省試第一。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the classified provincial examination of the first year of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the classified provincial examination of the first year of Longxing (1163).

sentences.zh: 虞允文宣撫四蜀，辟幹辦公事，入相，薦於朝。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen was pacification commissioner of the four Shu regions and recruited him as staff officer; when Yunwen entered the councilorship, he recommended him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen, pacification commissioner of the four Shu regions, recruited him as staff officer; when Yunwen entered the councilorship, he recommended him to court.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，召見便殿，孝宗大奇之，即日手詔除正字。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, he was summoned to audience in the informal hall; Xiaozong was greatly struck by him and that same day issued a handwritten edict appointing him collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao (1169), he was summoned to audience in the informal hall; Emperor Xiaozong was greatly struck by him and that same day issued a handwritten edict appointing him collator.

sentences.zh: 范成大使金，將行，雄當登對，允文招與之語。

translations.literal: Fan Chengda was envoy to Jin and was about to depart; Xiong was to have an audience; Yunwen summoned him and spoke with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda was envoy to Jin and was about to depart; Xiong was to have an audience; Yunwen summoned him and spoke with him.

sentences.zh: 既進見，雄極論恢復。

translations.literal: After entering audience, Xiong argued forcefully for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: After entering audience, Xiong argued forcefully for recovery.

sentences.zh: 孝宗大喜曰：「功名與卿共之。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong was greatly pleased and said: "Merit and fame I shall share with you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong was greatly pleased and said, "Merit and fame I shall share with you."

sentences.zh: 即除右史，兩月除舍人。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed right diarist, and two months later appointed drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed right diarist, and two months later appointed drafter.

sentences.zh: 金使耶律子敬賀會慶節，雄館伴。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy Yelü Zijing came to congratulate the Assembly Celebration Festival; Xiong served as host.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy Yelü Zijing came to congratulate the Assembly Celebration Festival; Xiong served as host.

sentences.zh: 子敬披露事情不敢隱，邏者以聞。

translations.literal: Zijing disclosed affairs and dared not conceal them; the patrol officers reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing disclosed affairs and dared not conceal them; the patrol officers reported this.

sentences.zh: 上夜召雄，雄具以子敬所言對，上喜。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xiong at night; Xiong fully reported what Zijing had said, and the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xiong at night; Xiong fully reported what Zijing had said, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 金使入辭，故事當用樂，雄奏：「卜郊有日，天子方齋，樂不可用。」

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy came to take leave, by precedent music should be used; Xiong memorialized: "The date for the suburban sacrifice has been chosen and the Son of Heaven is now fasting—music may not be used."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy came to take leave, by precedent music should be used; Xiong memorialized, "The date for the suburban sacrifice has been chosen and the Son of Heaven is now fasting—music may not be used."

sentences.zh: 上難之，遣中使諭雄，雄奏：「金使必不敢不順，即有他，臣得引與就館。」

translations.literal: The emperor found this difficult; he sent a palace envoy to instruct Xiong. Xiong memorialized: "The Jin envoy surely will not dare disobey; even if there is trouble, your servant can lead him to the guest lodge."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found this difficult; he sent a palace envoy to instruct Xiong. Xiong memorialized, "The Jin envoy surely will not dare disobey; even if there is trouble, I can lead him to the guest lodge."

sentences.zh: 上大喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 雄請復置恢復局，日夜講磨，條具合上意，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xiong requested reestablishment of the Recovery Bureau, worked day and night in deliberation, submitted proposals that matched the emperor's intent, and was appointed drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong requested reestablishment of the Recovery Bureau, worked day and night in deliberation, submitted proposals that matched the emperor's intent, and was appointed drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自選人入館至此，未滿歲也。

translations.literal: From entering the academy as a selected candidate to this point, not a full year had passed.
translations.idiomatic: From entering the academy as a selected candidate to this point, not a full year had passed.

sentences.zh: 時金將起河南之役，議盡以諸陵梓宮歸於我。

translations.literal: At that time Jin was about to launch a campaign in Henan; it was proposed that all the imperial coffins from the tombs be returned to us.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jin were about to launch a campaign in Henan; it was proposed that all the imperial coffins from the tombs be returned to us.

sentences.zh: 上命雄出使賀生辰，仍止奉遷陵寢及正受書儀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiong to go as envoy to congratulate the birthday and to limit his mission to requesting transfer of the tombs and correcting the protocol for receiving letters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xiong to go as envoy to congratulate the birthday and to limit his mission to requesting transfer of the tombs and correcting the protocol for receiving letters.

sentences.zh: 雄既見金主，爭辨數四。

translations.literal: After Xiong had audience with the Jin ruler, he argued back and forth several times.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiong had audience with the Jin ruler, he argued back and forth several times.

sentences.zh: 其臣屢喝起，雄辭益力，卒得請乃已，金人謂之「龍鬥」。

translations.literal: Jin ministers repeatedly shouted for him to rise, but Xiong's words grew only stronger; he finally obtained his request before stopping. The Jin called this a 'dragon fight.'
translations.idiomatic: Jin ministers repeatedly shouted for him to rise, but Xiong's words grew only stronger; he finally obtained his request before stopping. The Jin called this a "dragon fight."

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏論恢復計，大略謂：「莫若由蜀以取陝西，得陝西以臨中原，是秦制六國之勢也。」

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial discussing plans for recovery, saying in summary: "Nothing is better than taking Shaanxi through Shu; with Shaanxi in hand one can overlook the Central Plains—this is the posture of Qin controlling the six states."
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial discussing plans for recovery, saying in summary, "Nothing is better than taking Shaanxi through Shu; with Shaanxi in hand one can overlook the Central Plains—this is the posture of Qin controlling the six states."

sentences.zh: 八年，以母憂去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he left office on account of mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，召為禮部侍郎，除端明殿學士，簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, he was recalled as vice minister of rites, appointed academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi (1175), he was recalled as vice minister of rites, appointed academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 一日奏事，上曰：「今夏蠶麥甚熟、絲米價平可喜。」

translations.literal: One day while reporting on affairs, the emperor said: "This summer the silkworms and wheat ripened well and silk and grain prices are stable—this is cause for joy."
translations.idiomatic: One day while reporting on affairs, the emperor said, "This summer the silkworms and wheat ripened well and silk and grain prices are stable—this is cause for joy."

sentences.zh: 雄奏：「孟子論王道始於不饑不寒。」

translations.literal: Xiong memorialized: "Mencius said that the kingly way begins with freedom from hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied, "Mencius said that the kingly way begins with freedom from hunger and cold."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近世士大夫好高論，恥言農事，微有西晉風。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In recent times scholar-officials love lofty discourse and are ashamed to speak of farming—there is a slight whiff of Western Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In recent times scholar-officials love lofty discourse and are ashamed to speak of farming—there is a slight whiff of Western Jin.

sentences.zh: 豈知《周禮》與《易》言理財，周公、孔子曷嘗不以理財為務？

translations.literal: Do they not know that the Rites of Zhou and the Changes speak of managing wealth, and that the Duke of Zhou and Confucius ever took managing wealth as their task?
translations.idiomatic: Do they not know that the Rites of Zhou and the Changes speak of managing wealth, and that the Duke of Zhou and Confucius ever took managing wealth as their task?

sentences.zh: 且不獨此，士夫諱言恢復，不知其家有田百畝，內五十畝為人所據，亦投牒理索否？」

translations.literal: And not this alone—gentlemen avoid speaking of recovery, yet do they not know that if their family had a hundred mu of fields and fifty mu within were seized by others, they would still submit petitions to recover them?"
translations.idiomatic: And not this alone—gentlemen avoid speaking of recovery, yet do they not know that if their family had a hundred mu of fields and fifty mu within were seized by others, they would still submit petitions to recover them?"

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「陛下志在大有為，敢不布堯言，書之《時政記》。」

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Your Majesty's ambition is for great achievement—how dare I not spread these words of Yao and record them in the Record of Current Policy?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said, "Your Majesty's ambition is for great achievement—how dare I not spread these words of Yao and record them in the Record of Current Policy?"

sentences.zh: 十一月，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he was appointed associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, he was appointed associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, he was appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，拜右丞相。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he was appointed right chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, he was appointed right chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 每進見，必曰「二帝在沙漠」，未嘗離諸口也。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered audience, he always said 'the two emperors are in the desert'—these words never left his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered audience, he always said "the two emperors are in the desert"—these words never left his lips.

sentences.zh: 朱熹累召不出，雄請處以外郡，命知南康軍。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi was repeatedly summoned but would not come out; Xiong requested that he be placed in an outer commandery and was ordered to command Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi was repeatedly summoned but would not come out; Xiong requested that he be placed in an outer commandery and was ordered to command Nankang.

sentences.zh: 熹極論時事，上怒，諭雄令分析。

translations.literal: Xi argued forcefully on current affairs; the emperor was angry and instructed Xiong to analyze and refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued forcefully on current affairs; the emperor was angry and instructed Xiong to analyze and refute him.

sentences.zh: 雄奏：「熹狂生，詞窮理短，罪之適成其名。

translations.literal: Xiong memorialized: "Xi is a wild scholar; his words are exhausted and his reasoning weak—to punish him would only make his name.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong memorialized, "Xi is a wild scholar; his words are exhausted and his reasoning weak—to punish him would only make his name.

sentences.zh: 若天涵地育，置而不問可也。」

translations.literal: If Heaven covers and Earth nourishes, one may set him aside and not inquire further."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven covers and Earth nourishes, one may set him aside and not inquire further."

sentences.zh: 會周必大亦力言之，乃止。

translations.literal: At this time Zhou Bida also spoke forcefully on this point, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhou Bida also spoke forcefully on this point, and the matter was dropped.
